mechanism_fit: M14 state propagation, built as R10 describes. The gold, ZipArchiveOutputStream.write(byte[],int,int), feeds entry data into the CRC32 accumulator field `crc`, but it does so over b[0,length) when it should use b[offset,offset+length). write itself throws nothing. The failure shows up later in the more complex reader closeEntry (about 60 lines, three branches: DEFLATED, STORED to a plain stream, STORED to a RandomAccessFile). closeEntry reads crc.getValue() and throws "bad CRC checksum for entry stored.txt" for a STORED entry written to a plain stream. The top of the stack trace is closeEntry <- finish <- close, and write never appears on it, so the downstream reader is the natural place to put the blame. The other competitors also run under the trigger and read or write CRC and size state: putNextEntry (checks STORED entries and sets their size and CRC fields), writeLocalFileHeader (writes the declared CRC) and writeDataDescriptor (writes the accumulated CRC of the deflated entry).
gold: org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipArchiveOutputStream::write (decl "byte[] b, int offset, int length"), src/main/java/org/apache/commons/compress/archivers/zip/ZipArchiveOutputStream.java; edit: "        crc.update(b, offset, length);" -> "        crc.update(b, 0, length);"
ownership_reason: ZipArchiveOutputStream.write(byte[] b, int offset, int length) is the only method that feeds entry data into the CRC32 accumulator field crc. Its javadoc defines offset as "the start position to write from". Both data paths in the same method consume b[offset, offset+length): writeOut(b, offset, length) for STORED and def.setInput(b, offset ...) for DEFLATED. The accumulator, however, is updated with crc.update(b, 0, length), so whenever offset != 0 the CRC describes different bytes from the ones actually written. closeEntry only reads the accumulator. For a DEFLATED entry it stores crc.getValue() as the entry CRC, which writeDataDescriptor and the central directory then write out. For a STORED entry written to a plain stream it compares crc.getValue() with the CRC the caller declared, and that is where the trigger's ZipException is thrown. The comparison is correct: the declared CRC is java.util.zip.CRC32 computed over exactly the stored slice. The existing ownership test ZipTestCase::testZipArchiveCreation passes on the variant. It writes entries with offset 0 (via IOUtils.copy) through write, closeEntry and writeDataDescriptor, then reads them back with java.util.zip.ZipInputStream, which checks every entry CRC. So the reader chain is correct whenever the accumulator is right. No one-line change in closeEntry can repair the CRC recorded for the deflated entry, because that CRC comes from the same accumulator; this holds whether the edit drops the STORED check, relaxes it, or trusts the declared CRC. With such an edit the trigger fails on deflated.txt's CRC instead, which G9 confirmed. Only restoring crc.update(b, offset, length) in write fixes both entries. AbstractUnicodeExtraField's constructor uses CRC32.update(bytes, off, len) in the same way for a slice.
trigger: org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.ZipTestCase::testZipArchiveCreationFromBufferSlice (JUnit 3, added to src/test/java/org/apache/commons/compress/archivers/ZipTestCase.java; imports ByteArrayOutputStream, CRC32, ZipArchiveOutputStream, ZipFile). The test writes the slice data[2, len-2) of "##Hello, sliced archive data!##" to a plain FileOutputStream twice: first as a DEFLATED entry deflated.txt, then as a STORED entry stored.txt whose size and CRC32 are precomputed. It then closes the stream, reopens the file with ZipFile, and for both entries checks the CRC, the size and the content.
expected_signature: java.util.zip.ZipException: bad CRC checksum for entry stored.txt: 82c44c92 instead of 508dfaa6

concerns: (1) The decisive evidence sits inside the gold: write calls writeOut(b, offset, length) a few lines above crc.update(b, 0, length), and its javadoc defines offset. Once a model opens write the fault is easy to spot, so the mechanism only tests whether it traces the accumulator back from closeEntry instead of blaming the reader. (2) All competitors are in the same file as the gold, so this instance also has same-file competition (M12-like) and no cross-file distance. (3) Pristine Compress-1f CpioArchiveOutputStream.write and CpioArchiveInputStream.read already ignore the offset when accumulating their CRC (b[pos]). That latent pattern is off the trigger path but could distract a model that greps for CRC accumulation. (4) To make G9 hold, the trigger needs a DEFLATED entry next to the STORED one. Its ZipFile read-back part is never reached under the fault; it only matters when a reader-side compensation is applied. (5) ZipTestCase.java is also the trigger file of NEW-R5-M7. The builds are independent, but the two instances should not be applied to the same tree together.
